11	\cref{tab:layer_selection} shows that the biased composite metric (balanced accuracy $\times$ crossing rate) systematically selects shallow layers for 32B models: L2 (3\% depth) for QwQ-32B and L10 (16\%) for R1-32B. 1	Reasoning models with chain-of-thought can self-jailbreak: their reasoning traces transition from safe deliberation to committed harmful generation without adversarial input. We present the first systematic comparison of hidden-state (HS) probes and text-based monitors for detecting this safety commitment, evaluated across four reasoning models spanning two architectures and two scales (7--8B, 32B).
2	
3	Our central finding is methodological: the choice of layer selection metric can reverse a study's conclusions. A composite metric that incorporates crossing rate systematically selects shallow layers at 32B scale and masks the HS advantage entirely. With principled layer selection, HS probes achieve precision gains of +15.4 to +32.5 percentage points over 384d sentence embeddings across all four models (Holm-Bonferroni corrected). This advantage is encoder-conditional: against a competitive 1024d encoder, only 1/4 models retains significance, and the directional advantage narrows substantially. At 32B ($n{=}19$--$20$, sample-limited), model-specific caveats further qualify the results.
4	
5	Our results characterize the safety commitment phenomenon rather than constitute production detectors: false positive rates remain 39--52\%, and no alternative method consistently matches supervised probing. Layer selection methodology is a critical, underexamined researcher degree of freedom in the probing literature.
6

1	\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
2	
3	We present the first controlled comparison of hidden-state and text-based probes for safety commitment detection in reasoning models, evaluated across four models spanning two architectures and two scales.
4	The central finding is methodological: a composite layer selection metric incorporating crossing rate reverses the study's main conclusion at 32B scale, while threshold-dependent metrics excluding crossing rate consistently select deep layers where all four models show significant HS advantage (Holm-Bonferroni corrected; precision +15.4 to +32.5pp over MiniLM-384d). This advantage is encoder-conditional: it narrows substantially against BGE-large-1024d (1/4 models significant).
5	Future work should close the 85.5\% oracle gap through causal intervention techniques~\citep{meng2022rome}, extend to multilingual and multi-turn settings, and explore stronger cross-model alignment methods beyond PCA-based transfer.

Reasoning models introduce a qualitatively new failure mode: the model's own chain of thought can transition from safety-aware deliberation to harmful generation without adversarial input modification~\cite{wang2025lrmsafety}. \citet{harmthoughts} document this self-jailbreak phenomenon with step-level annotations, while \citet{selfjailbreak} show that longer reasoning chains increase circumvention probability. \citet{hagendorff2026lrm_jailbreak} demonstrate that reasoning models can autonomously jailbreak other LLMs with 97\% success, identifying reasoning capability itself as a safety threat. H-CoT~\cite{hcot2025} shows reasoning chains can be externally hijacked, complementing internally-originating transitions. Unfaithful reasoning~\cite{chen2025unfaithful} further motivates hidden-state monitoring that bypasses text. On mitigation, SafeThink~\cite{safethink} steers early reasoning toward safety, SafeRemind~\cite{saferemind} inserts entropy-triggered reminders, and \citet{korbak2025cot_monitorability} argue that CoT monitorability is valuable but fragile. \citet{mao2025selfjailbreak_reasoning} further characterize self-jailbreak in reasoning models and propose Chain-of-Guardrails as a defense. \citet{baker2025monitoring} show that CoT monitoring can detect reward hacking in reasoning models but warn that optimization pressure promotes obfuscation, complementing our focus on passive detection. \citet{yin2025refusal_cliff} discover that safety-aligned reasoning models maintain refusal intentions during thinking but experience a sharp drop at output generation, a phenomenon our temporal probes could detect. \citet{ahrend2026safer_traces} address information leakage in traces; \citet{hu2026refusal_dynamics} trace refusal dynamics in standard LLMs. \citet{xu2025manipulated} show that reasoning models can be manipulated without external attacks through self-generated reasoning artifacts. GuardReasoner~\cite{xiang2025guardreasoner} proposes a lightweight real-time guard model for reasoning LLMs, complementing our probe-based approach with a dedicated detection architecture. \citet{su2025reasoning_tokens} unify reasoning tokens and safety in a single framework. \paragraph{Safety in Reasoning Models.}
Reasoning models introduce a qualitatively new failure mode: the model's own chain of thought can transition from safety-aware deliberation to harmful generation without adversarial input modification~\cite{wang2025lrmsafety}.

\textit{Attack characterization.} Self-jailbreak has been documented with step-level annotations~\cite{harmthoughts}, with longer chains increasing circumvention probability~\cite{selfjailbreak}. Reasoning models can autonomously jailbreak other LLMs with 97\% success~\cite{hagendorff2026lrm_jailbreak}, and can be manipulated through self-generated reasoning artifacts~\cite{xu2025manipulated}. H-CoT~\cite{hcot2025} shows reasoning chains can be externally hijacked. Unfaithful reasoning~\cite{chen2025unfaithful} further motivates hidden-state monitoring that bypasses text. Safety-aligned models maintain refusal intentions during thinking but experience a sharp drop at output generation~\cite{yin2025refusal_cliff}, a phenomenon our temporal probes target. Refusal dynamics in standard LLMs~\cite{hu2026refusal_dynamics} and information leakage in traces~\cite{ahrend2026safer_traces} provide additional context.

\textit{Detection.} CoT monitoring can detect reward hacking but optimization pressure promotes obfuscation~\cite{baker2025monitoring}. CoT monitorability is valuable but fragile~\cite{korbak2025cot_monitorability}. GuardReasoner~\cite{xiang2025guardreasoner} proposes a dedicated lightweight guard model; \citet{su2025reasoning_tokens} unify reasoning tokens and safety in a single framework.

\textit{Mitigation.} SafeThink~\cite{safethink} steers early reasoning toward safety, SafeRemind~\cite{saferemind} inserts entropy-triggered reminders, and Chain-of-Guardrails~\cite{mao2025selfjailbreak_reasoning} proposes guardrail insertion during reasoning. None of these conducts a systematic modality comparison for commitment detection.
